characters.title: 偷听瓢虫
characters.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: four-frame 2D game sprite animation sheet, EDIT of the attached approved character portrait. The input image is the EXACT character model, not a loose style reference. Preserve its identity, proportions, anatomy, face construction, dark pixel outline, stepped pixel clusters, warm soft internal shading, exact palette and all signature details. Do not redesign, simplify, change species, add clothing or change the rendering style. Do not replace the character with a generic bat. This is gentle pixel artwork as in the attached original.
Output ONE square transparent sprite sheet, EXACTLY 2 columns by 2 rows, no gaps between the equal square cells, but generous transparent padding inside each cell. Four frames in reading order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. Only one complete character per cell, no labels, text, panel borders, decorative floor or background. Keep exactly the same character size, stable head/body proportions, foot baseline and camera view in all four frames. Fit the entire character including long appendages inside each cell. Aim for character height around 80% of a cell. Actual transparent alpha outside the character/explicit action prop. Crisp pixel-art edges, no blur, no 3D or vector restyling. Small localized articulated motion, never whole-character squashing or stretching. Character invariants: the exact small dusty mauve furry oval bat from input, disproportionately gigantic asymmetric ears (viewer-left tall cream-lined ear with a curled tip; viewer-right shorter tightly curled loop ear), tiny cream membrane wings, little feet, cream heart-shaped chest patch, blushing face with small oval eyes and tiny open pink mouth. The head/body is tiny relative to ears. Preserve the cream lining, ear thickness, ear lengths and asymmetry throughout. The big ears are flexible ears, not horns, ribbons, antennae or separate objects.
Action: "Ladybird Listen", a curious little radar hears a ladybird walking on a leaf. A tiny leaf with a red ladybird sits to the viewer-right of the feet, never overlaps the body. Frame 1 reproduce the original portrait pose and expression as exactly as possible, with this tiny leaf/bug beside it. Frame 2 body holds perfectly still, pupils notice the bug; the shorter curled ear turns slightly toward the leaf, the very tall ear remains unmistakably long and curled. Frame 3 both ears angle gently toward the tiny bug; the taller ear bends a little near its tip only, never becomes shorter, the face is attentively listening. Frame 4 ears gently begin to return to their original angles as the bug takes another step; tiny surprised mouth. A quiet attentive action, not jumping, dancing or body deformation.
